situation.note: sem exams in 3 weeks and i cant focus for even 20 min, keep opening insta, and then at night i think papa paid 2 lakh for coaching and im wasting it

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call a mind that won't settle, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from a mind that won't settle to a mind that can hold still for twenty minutes.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the restlessness and the guilt, named without judgement.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the phone and the replaying are the same thing: a mind that has never been given one quiet minute.
week_beats.steady: You hold that your worth is not the exam, and the effort is yours.
week_beats.act: You try one ten-minute practice to steady the mind before you open the book.
week_beats.story: A student before a great exam shows you how to hold the mind still and find the focus.

understanding.core_struggle: Three weeks from exams, she can't focus, opens Instagram, and feels she is wasting the two lakh her father paid for coaching.
understanding.mirror: You sit down to study and open Instagram, then lie awake at night replaying the two lakh your father paid.
understanding.insight: The two lakh is real, but the mind that can't focus is not your fault. It is a mind that has never been trained to rest.

queries.hook: The weight of an exam three weeks away and a mind that won't settle, replaying every rupee your father spent on you.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: Praise and blame come and go, but what is yours cannot be taken; the effort is yours and the result is not.
queries.act: Practise steadying the mind for ten minutes before you open the book; let the result go and give the work its full attention.
queries.story: A student before a great exam, whose mind runs wild until he learns to hold it, and finds the focus to pass.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna looks at Krishna and says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. He says it is as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees that the mind is difficult to control, but he says practice and letting go can train it.
verse.for_you: Three weeks before your exams and your mind keeps opening Instagram. You feel ashamed about the two lakh your father paid for coaching. The mind that jumps from one thing to the next is not a flaw in you. It is a mind that has simply not learned to rest.
verse.try_today: When you open Instagram, notice the restlessness and close the app without guilt.
verse.scene_line: You are standing before your teacher, confessing that your mind is as hard to hold as the wind.
asks: How do I stop the mind from jumping to Instagram?

verse.speaker: Nidagha
verse.sanskrit: इतश्चेतश्च सुव्यग्रं व्यर्थमेवाभिधावति । मनो दूरतरं याति ग्रामे कौलेयको यथा ॥
verse.line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
verse.translation: The mind runs here and there, restless and pointless; it wanders far away, like a dog in a village.
verse.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

verse.for_you: The mind runs here and there for nothing. The phone is just the village street where it wanders, and the shame is the leash pulling you back. What you are doing is not wasting the two lakh.
verse.try_today: Notice the mind running without feeding it.
verse.scene_line: You are the teacher and the student, watching a stray mind in a village street.
asks: How do I train a mind that has never rested?
Can I stop feeling ashamed of the wandering?

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: Rules of conduct for a renunciant.
verse.sanskrit: नात्यर्थं सुखदुःखाभ्यां शरीरमुपतायेत् । स्तूयमानो न तुषेत निन्दितो न शपेत्परान् ॥
verse.line: Don't wear out your body chasing pleasure or fleeing pain. Praised, don't gloat; blamed, don't curse others.
verse.translation: Let him not torment the body too much for the sake of pleasure or pain. Praised, let him not gloat; blamed, let him not curse others.
verse.meaning: A teacher is laying down the rules for a person who has left the world behind. The teacher says do not wear out your body chasing pleasure or fleeing pain. When people praise you, do not let it swell your chest. When they blame you, do not let it send you into a rage against others. The point is to stop swinging between extremes. Your body and your mind are not tools to punish yourself with.
verse.for_you: You are not the exam and the two lakh is not the measure of your worth. The effort is yours alone. When your parents check in, you can see their care without letting it become a weight. Your worth is not in the result.
verse.try_today: Notice when you are chasing a distraction or running from a thought.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own room, caught between the lure of the phone and the fear of the exam.
asks: How do I stop the phone from pulling me away?
Why does my mind feel so heavy right now?
What does my body need when I cannot focus?

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verse.sanskrit: नैव प्रार्थयते लाभं नालाभेनानुशोचति । धीरस्य शीतलं चित्तममृतेनैव पूरितम् ॥
verse.line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
verse.translation: He does not pray for gain, nor grieve over loss. The steady one's cool mind is filled as if with nectar.
verse.why: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

matched.label: I'm anxious about how things will turn out

prasang.title: The calm of the wise
prasang.summary: In a hundred verses Ashtavakra paints the inner peace of the wise: calm while busy, unmoved by gain or loss, praise or blame, at ease whether in the city or the forest. The restless, by contrast, chase peace and never find it.
prasang.lesson: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka about the calm of the wise. He says a steady person does not beg for gain or grieve over loss. Their mind stays cool and full as if filled with nectar. The verse points out that calm is not found by chasing it or changing places. It is simply how you hold ordinary life.
verse.for_you: The two lakh your father paid is a weight, but your worth is not the exam. Your effort is yours. The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog, and you feel ashamed. You are not the dog.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when the mind stops running, even for a second, and let it sit there.
verse.scene_line: You are the one who notices the dog, not the dog itself.
asks: How do I stop feeling like the exam is my whole worth?
What does it mean to hold my effort without the result?
Can the mind be full even when I am anxious?

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha on effort and grace, after Prahlada's story.
verse.sanskrit: नित्याभ्यासविवेकाभ्यां चित्तमाशु प्रसीदति । आम्र एव दशामेति साहकारीं शनैः शनैः ॥
verse.line: Daily practice and clear thinking make the mind clear, slowly, the way a mango ripens.
verse.translation: Through daily practice and discernment the mind soon becomes clear, just as a mango slowly ripens into its sweetness.
verse.why: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Prahlada: effort and grace are not rivals
prasang.summary: After telling how Prahlada awakened, Vasishtha faces Rama's challenge: if everything comes by effort, wasn't Prahlada saved by Vishnu's grace? Vasishtha answers that Prahlada earned it himself, that the Self and Vishnu are not two, and that sometimes we wake by our own effort and sometimes by grace reached through devotion. Steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango.
prasang.lesson: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha tells Rama that through daily practice and clear thinking, the mind becomes clear slowly, just as a mango ripens into its sweetness. He is speaking to Rama after the story of Prahlada, to show that grace and effort are not rivals. The teaching is that you could keep practising every day, and allow your mind to ripen in its own time rather than forcing it.
verse.for_you: You are waiting for focus to arrive all at once, but your mind is like that mango, needing daily practice to ripen. The restlessness you feel is not a sign of failure. Each time you open the book and return to it, you are doing the work.
verse.try_today: Sit with your book for ten minutes before you check your phone today.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own kitchen, with a book and a mango on the table.
asks: How do I keep my hands off the phone when the book feels heavy?
What does daily practice look like when I can barely focus for five minutes?
Can the mind really ripen if I keep failing to sit still?

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verse.sanskrit: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
verse.line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
verse.translation: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
verse.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

verse.meaning: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion. Rama tells him to sit in a quiet place, let the senses rest, and give full attention to one thing. The mind, he says, will become still and clear, like a still ocean, if you rest in faith and keep your attention on one thing.
verse.for_you: The two lakhs are real, and the weight of them is heavy on you. But the mind that runs to Instagram is not your fault. It is a mind that has never been taught to rest. Rama tells Lakshmana to sit quietly and let the senses rest.
verse.try_today: Sit in a quiet place for ten minutes and let your senses rest before you open the book.
verse.scene_line: You are sitting in a quiet place, letting your senses rest before the next wave of thought.
asks: How do I sit quietly when my mind wants to run?
Can I really rest my senses when the exams are so close?

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.
